questions.question: Describe about Earthquake risk factors / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Earthquake Risk Factors
  • Population Density – More people in an area means more damage and deaths.
  • Building Quality – Weak or old buildings collapse easily during earthquakes.
  • Emergency Preparedness – Good rescue systems and public awareness reduce loss of life.
  • Tectonic Activity – Places near fault zones are more likely to experience earthquakes.
  • Ground Conditions – Soft soil can increase shaking and cause liquefaction.
  • Secondary Hazards – Earthquakes can also cause landslides, tsunamis, fires, floods, and aftershocks.

questions.question: Explain the process of cyclone formation, focusing on the role of warm air, moisture, and the Coriolis Effect. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Cyclones form over warm oceans where the air becomes warm and moist.
  • The warm air rises, creating a low-pressure area, and more air moves in.
  • As the air rises, it cools and condenses, forming clouds and releasing heat, which makes the system
  • stronger.
  • The Coriolis Effect (due to Earth’s rotation) causes the winds to spin around the low-pressure centre,
  • forming a cyclone.
